title: Applicability of the QUIC Transport Protocol (RFC 9308)
purpose: Capture the implementation-relevant RFC 9308 applicability guidance as informational SpecTrace items without creating speculative protocol features.
scope: This specification covers public API guidance, application-developer documentation, flow-control and stream-limit backpressure proof, application close-code propagation, migration/NAT rebinding observability, version/deployment boundaries, and DATAGRAM applicability boundaries for the current QUIC and HTTP/3 implementation.
context: RFC 9308 is informational. Requirements in this artifact are applicability and support-boundary requirements for this repository. They do not supersede RFC 9000, RFC 9001, RFC 9002, RFC 9114, RFC 9204, RFC 9221, RFC 9287, RFC 9368, or RFC 9369 protocol requirements.

requirements.title: Keep public application 0-RTT profile gated
requirements.statement: Public application 0-RTT MUST remain unavailable until an application profile defines replay-safe early-data semantics.

requirements.title: Separate keep-alive from resumption
requirements.statement: Application-facing documentation MUST distinguish connection keep-alive behavior from TLS session resumption and 0-RTT application data.

requirements.title: Document application stream mapping
requirements.statement: Application protocols MUST explicitly map QUIC streams to their protocol roles and message boundaries.

requirements.title: Expose flow-control blocked backpressure
requirements.statement: Application send paths that become flow-control blocked MUST preserve stream state and expose blocked-credit diagnostics.

requirements.title: Expose stream-limit blocked backpressure
requirements.statement: Application stream-open paths that become stream-limit blocked MUST preserve stream state and expose blocked-stream diagnostics.

requirements.title: Keep application close codes separate
requirements.statement: Application close error codes MUST remain distinct from QUIC transport error codes.

requirements.title: Validate migration candidates before promotion
requirements.statement: NAT rebinding and migration candidates MUST remain unpromoted until path validation succeeds.

requirements.title: Document connection ID privacy boundary
requirements.statement: Application-facing documentation MUST describe the supported connection-ID privacy boundary without claiming broader timing-linkability mitigation.

requirements.title: Document version deployment boundary
requirements.statement: Application-facing documentation MUST distinguish implemented version-negotiation mechanisms from operator rollout policy for new QUIC versions.

requirements.title: Document DATAGRAM applicability boundary
requirements.statement: Application-facing documentation MUST distinguish the RFC 9221 QUIC DATAGRAM transport floor from HTTP Datagrams, CONNECT-UDP, and MASQUE behavior.

supplemental_sections.heading: Informational Classification
supplemental_sections.content: RFC 9308 sections 2, 5, 7, 8.1, 10, 12, and parts of 11 and 14 are treated as deployment, documentation, or observability guidance for this repository unless another RFC family supplies a concrete protocol requirement. Item-level classification is maintained in `docs/design/rfc9308-rfc9312-spectrace-classification.md`.

supplemental_sections.heading: Deferred Or Not Applicable Items
supplemental_sections.content: Automatic fallback, public application 0-RTT, HTTP/3 priority signaling, Alt-Svc/SVCB endpoint discovery, public DSCP controls, HTTP Datagrams, CONNECT-UDP, MASQUE, and QUIC-LB/server-redirection behavior are not implemented by this applicability slice.
